work_order.understanding: The release-notes gate packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs checks category presence, category membership, authors presence, authors-is-an-array, and a one-line body. It never inspects an author value, so `authors: [claude]` passes the gate that exists to keep the published changelog honest and ships to readers as `— thanks @claude`. Re-verified the defect and the whole fix against the real repository this time, not a clone: on a scratch branch taken from the current HEAD, carrying the prototype change plus a temporary note whose only author is `claude`, the real script printed `::error::Release note upcoming-release-notes/tmp-bot-author.md authors must be GitHub usernames of people, not bots or agents: claude.` and exited 1; with the gate reverted to origin/main and the identical note in place, the same command printed `Validated 1 release note(s). 🎉` and exited 0. The issue's proposed handle-shape check cannot catch this: `claude` is a syntactically perfect GitHub handle, and all 39 distinct author values in the directory pass such a rule. The owner's recorded decision is binding and this plan implements it exactly: credit Shivam-Fl on both shipped notes, and reject agents/bots by a small denylist — `claude`, `github-actions`, and anything ending in `[bot]` case-insensitively — with a test per rule plus a test that Shivam-Fl passes, and no network lookup. The previous plan was rejected on one mechanical defect only, in the verification recipes: it branched the scratch branch from `origin/main`, which at QA time is unpatched, so AC-6 was unsatisfiable. That is fixed below and re-run against the real repository.
work_order.root_cause: validateFile asserts only that `authors` is present and an array; the value of each element is never examined, so any string — a bot login, a first name, a product name — passes the gate that exists to keep the published changelog honest.
work_order.approach: Two halves, one slice. (1) Put the identity rule in a pure, exported, unit-testable helper called from validateFile. It lives in packages/ci-actions/src/release-notes/util.mjs — the existing shared home for release-notes helpers that the check script already imports from — so no new module for one function. The rule is a denylist exactly as decided: lowercase+trim each author, reject if it equals `claude` or `github-actions` or ends in `[bot]` (which already covers `claude[bot]` and `github-actions[bot]`, the logins git history actually shows). The new branch goes after the `Array.isArray(data.authors)` check and before the one-line body check, preserving the existing ordering. (2) Correct the two shipped notes to `authors: [Shivam-Fl]` by editing in place — they are on main. The helper returns the offending values rather than a boolean so the error names what was wrong and what to put instead. No network call: the decision rules it out, and account existence could not distinguish `claude` (not an account) from `Shivam-Fl` (a real account that asked for the change rather than writing it) anyway. Applied the whole change on a scratch branch in this repository, ran the real gate against it five times, then deleted the branch and every probe artifact; `main` is back at 4ebaf1e with a clean tree.

files.change: Add an exported `NON_PERSON_AUTHORS` denylist (`['claude', 'github-actions']`) and an exported `findNonPersonAuthors(authors)` that returns the offending entries: lowercase+trim each author, keep it if it is in the denylist or matches /\[bot\]$/. Return an array (empty when every author is a person) rather than a boolean, so the caller can name the bad values in its error. Put it beside `categoryAutocorrections`/`categoryOrder`, which the check script already imports from here. Add a short comment saying why this is a denylist and not a shape check — `claude` is a valid GitHub handle, so only the identity list distinguishes the tool from the person — and that the small size is deliberate, since the network lookup was rejected as slow and token-dependent. Do not touch `parseReleaseNotes` or anything else in this file.
files.why: The check script is a top-level script with side effects (reads env, fetches git, exits) and cannot be imported by a test. util.mjs is the module it already imports for its other two validation constants, so the rule is testable and the diff is one import line.

files.change: In `validateFile`, after the existing `Array.isArray(data.authors)` branch and before the `trimmedContent` check, add: `const nonPersonAuthors = findNonPersonAuthors(data.authors); if (nonPersonAuthors.length > 0) { reportError(`Release note ${path} authors must be GitHub usernames of people, not bots or agents: ${nonPersonAuthors.join(', ')}.`); return false; }`. Add `findNonPersonAuthors` to the existing named import from `../src/release-notes/util.mjs`. Keep the failure message naming the rejected values so the author knows what to replace them with. Change nothing else in this file.

acceptance.check: End to end: the real gate rejects a note whose only author is 'claude'. Running the check on a scratch branch whose single new commit adds a note with `authors: [claude]` prints `::error::` naming `claude` and exits non-zero, where the same branch printed `Validated 1 release note(s).` and exited 0 before this change.
acceptance.how_to_verify: BRANCH FROM THE CURRENT HEAD, which carries the fix — `git checkout -b scratch/rn-check` with no start point. Do not branch from origin/main: at QA time this change is on the unmerged PR branch while origin/main is still 4ebaf1e with the unpatched gate, so `git checkout -b scratch/rn-check origin/main` would drop the change under test and run the gate that passes. Confirmed here: `git rev-parse main origin/main HEAD` returned 4ebaf1e95b51e305b995074125a294e605c54053 for all three before the change, and `git show origin/main:packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs | grep findNonPersonAuthors` returns nothing. BASE_REF stays `main` — a branch name, never a SHA: the script does `git fetch origin $BASE_REF` then `git diff origin/$BASE_REF...HEAD`, and a raw-SHA fetch writes only FETCH_HEAD, creating no refs/remotes/origin/<sha>, so `origin/<sha>` does not resolve and the script dies before validateFile runs. GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY must be exported on every invocation: reportError pipes README.md into `fs.createWriteStream(process.env.GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY)`, which throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE when unset. So: `git checkout -b scratch/rn-check`; add `upcoming-release-notes/tmp-bot-author.md` with front matter `category: Bugfix` / `authors: [claude]` and a single-line body; commit it as the only new commit (pre-commit hook runs nano-staged; use a subject starting with `[AI]`); then `BASE_REF=main GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY=/tmp/rn-summary.md node packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs`. Expect a non-zero exit and `::error::Release note upcoming-release-notes/tmp-bot-author.md authors must be GitHub usernames of people, not bots or agents: claude.` Then `git checkout main && git branch -D scratch/rn-check` and remove /tmp/rn-summary.md and the temporary note. Ran exactly this recipe in THIS repository on a scratch branch off HEAD: it produced that error line and exit 1; with the two source files reverted to origin/main and the identical note in place it printed `Validated 1 release note(s). 🎉` and exit 0. Only the temporary note is validated by these runs: the gate selects notes with `git diff --diff-filter=A origin/main...HEAD`, and this PR's two note corrections are modifications (M), which that filter excludes — confirmed `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=A origin/main...HEAD -- upcoming-release-notes/` returns only `tmp-bot-author.md` on that branch. (AC-1..AC-5 are the automated coverage; this step proves the wiring from validateFile to the helper, which no unit test reaches.)

The wiring proof (AC-6/AC-8). Two mechanical details, both of which have already cost a plan review, so state them plainly before running anything. (1) BRANCH FROM THE CURRENT HEAD: `git checkout -b scratch/rn-check` with NO start point. At QA time the fix is on this unmerged PR branch and `origin/main` still carries the unpatched gate — branching from origin/main silently tests nothing. (2) BASE_REF must be the string `main`, never a SHA: the script resolves `origin/$BASE_REF`, a raw-SHA fetch writes only FETCH_HEAD and no refs/remotes/origin/<sha>, so `git diff` aborts with 'ambiguous argument' before any validation runs. And export GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY every time, including the run expected to succeed: reportError pipes README.md into fs.createWriteStream(process.env.GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY), which throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE when unset. Sequence: `git checkout -b scratch/rn-check`; write upcoming-release-notes/tmp-bot-author.md with `category: Bugfix`, `authors: [claude]`, one-line body; commit (subject must start with `[AI]`; the pre-commit hook runs nano-staged); confirm the branch carries the fix with `git show HEAD:packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs | grep findNonPersonAuthors` (it must print a line) before trusting any result; run `BASE_REF=main GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY=/tmp/rn-summary.md node packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs` — expect non-zero exit and `::error::` naming `claude`; then edit the note to `authors: [Shivam-Fl]`, commit, run the identical command — expect `Validated 1 release note(s). 🎉` and exit 0. Sanity-check the selection with `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=A origin/main...HEAD -- upcoming-release-notes/`, which must print only the temporary note: the PR's two note corrections are modifications and --diff-filter=A excludes them, so this recipe validates the temporary note alone and says nothing about those two files — AC-7 covers them by grep. Finally `git checkout main && git branch -D scratch/rn-check` and remove the temporary note and /tmp/rn-summary.md. All of the above was run in this repository against a prototype of this change, with these exact outputs, and the branch and every probe artifact were then deleted.
risks: The denylist is a denylist: `copilot`, `cursor-agent`, `codex` or any future agent login still passes. The owner chose this explicitly over a network lookup, so it is a decision to carry, not a gap to route around — say so in the code comment so the next person does not mistake it for an oversight.

No such account appears in the 39 distinct author values in the directory, and the error names the value so it is diagnosable, but the failure mode is a red CI on an honest PR.

review.title: findNonPersonAuthors calls author.toLowerCase() with no type guard, so a note whose authors list contains a non-string crashes the gate with an unhandled TypeError instead of producing a reportError. The crash escapes the async IIFE at release-notes-check.mjs:80, so the process dies with a stack trace, GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY is never written, and no ::error:: annotation appears on the PR — a strictly worse failure mode than the one the gate already had for a malformed authors value.
review.detail:
findNonPersonAuthors calls author.toLowerCase() with no type guard, so a note whose authors list contains a non-string crashes the gate with an unhandled TypeError instead of producing a reportError. The crash escapes the async IIFE at release-notes-check.mjs:80, so the process dies with a stack trace, GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY is never written, and no ::error:: annotation appears on the PR — a strictly worse failure mode than the one the gate already had for a malformed authors value.

`packages/ci-actions/src/release-notes/util.mjs:41`

Evidence: Real script, real repo, scratch branch off HEAD carrying the PR. `printf -- '---\ncategory: Bugfix\nauthors: [123]\n---\n\nNumeric author probe.\n'` committed, then `BASE_REF=main GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY=/tmp/rn-sum2.md node packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs`. Output tail: `at findNonPersonAuthors (…/src/release-notes/util.mjs:41:18)` / `at validateFile (…/bin/release-notes-check.mjs:63:28)` / `at …release-notes-check.mjs:108:10`, exit 1. /tmp/rn-sum2.md was NOT created — reportError never ran. Same for `authors: [claude, null]` -> `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'toLowerCase')`, and for `[{name:'claude'}]` and `[['claude']]`. gray-matter parses bare `123` as a number and `null` as null, so these are reachable from hand-edited front matter; the pre-change gate validated only `Array.isArray` and let such a note through to publish `— thanks @123`.

Fix: Filter to strings before normalizing, e.g. `authors.filter(a => typeof a === 'string').filter(...)`, or coerce with `String(author).toLowerCase().trim()`. Better still, reject non-string entries explicitly so the author gets an actionable ::error:: rather than a crash or a silent publish.

review.title: The comment on the empty-list test states that a non-empty authors list is 'enforced by the missing/array checks in the check script'. That is false: `authors: []` passes both checks and the note ships crediting nobody.

`packages/ci-actions/src/release-notes/util.test.js:44`

Evidence: Node confirms `![] === false` and `Array.isArray([]) === true`, so release-notes-check.mjs:55 (`if (!data.authors)`) and :59 (`if (!Array.isArray(...))`) both fall through for an empty array. Real script on a scratch branch with `authors: []`: `Validated 1 release note(s). 🎉`, exit 0. The publisher then emits `- Empty-list probe note. — thanks ` — a dangling 'thanks' with no name. The test's assertion (findNonPersonAuthors([]) === []) is correct; only the stated reason is wrong, and a future reader will rely on it.

Fix: Either correct the comment to say the empty case is unhandled here, or close the gap in the gate with `if (data.authors.length === 0)` reporting 'is missing authors' — which would also fix the dangling-thanks publish. The latter is a pre-existing bug this PR did not introduce.

A's evidence describes the crash correctly but locates it only in hand-edited notes, which understates how easily a contributor hits it.
review.detail:
The non-string author crash A found at util.mjs:42 is reachable through the documented `yarn generate:release-notes` flow, not only through hand-edited front matter — so it is a first-class input, not a curiosity. A's evidence describes the crash correctly but locates it only in hand-edited notes, which understates how easily a contributor hits it.

`bin/release-note-generator.mts:25`

Evidence: bin/release-note-generator.mts:25 prompts 'Comma-separated GitHub username(s)' with `type: 'text'` and — unlike the filename and category prompts immediately below it — no `validate` (grep -n 'validate' over the file returns exactly one hit, line 34, the filename regex). getFileContents (line 147) interpolates the raw answer straight into `authors: [${username}]`. Typing a purely numeric handle at that prompt is enough: I took the exact string that function emits for username `123` and parsed it — `authors parsed: [123] | types: number`. A comma-separated answer does it too: `alice, 123` parses to `["alice",123] | types: string,number`, so a genuine contributor who fat-fingers one entry of an otherwise valid list crashes the gate. Both then hit findNonPersonAuthors and throw, as A demonstrated. The generator is the path the docs tell every contributor to use (packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md:111).

Fix: Add a `validate` to the username prompt in bin/release-note-generator.mts alongside the existing filename one, requiring non-empty comma-separated GitHub handles — that stops the bad value at the point of entry and gives the contributor an actionable message rather than a CI stack trace. The type guard at util.mjs:42 is still worth adding independently; the two are complementary, not alternatives.

Add a *.md file describing your change.` and exits 1. The severity is minor for that reason alone — it is a latent inconsistency, not a red build.

Fix: Either add a `Maintenance` note describing the gate change, or record in the PR that this change is deliberately note-exempt because it only edits existing notes. If the intent is for the gate to run here, wiring .github/actions/release-notes/check into a workflow is the larger piece of work and belongs in its own PR — it is a reserved path here.

review.title: `NON_PERSON_AUTHORS` is exported but has no importers — the new public surface is unused, and a future edit that adds a third caller would be the first, not the second.
review.detail:

`packages/ci-actions/src/release-notes/util.mjs:31`

Evidence: `grep -rn 'NON_PERSON_AUTHORS' --include=*.mjs --include=*.js --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx .` (excluding node_modules) returns two hits, both inside util.mjs: the declaration at line 31 and the single use inside findNonPersonAuthors at line 44. Nothing imports it. The module is imported by three real callers (bin/release-notes-check.mjs, bin/release-notes-generate.mjs, packages/docs/scripts/generate-upcoming-release-notes.mjs) and none of them reference the constant.

Fix: Drop the `export` and make it a module-private const. If the intent is for it to be configurable or reusable, that intent should land with the caller rather than as a dangling export. This is the only over-engineering in the diff — the rest of the design is proportionate: one constant, one regex, one small pure function, and a call site that reads in three lines.
